akash: Heads-up — canary group (5.1.2-rc) is showing ~2x decode p95 on long-tail requests (seq > 1024). CI alerted at 03:12 UTC. Can someone take a look? :eyes:

release-bot: Rollout paused for that canary group until triage completes.

ci-bot: perf-regression alert: job=perf/latency-canary, metric=decode_p95, delta=+95%, trace=http://ci/redwood/trace/1718002468

emma: I pulled a canary node and ran a quick profile. Two big observations: KV cache hit rate dropped from ~0.98 -> 0.64, and avg batch size fell from ~4.8 -> ~2.1. Both would explain higher tail latency.

lucas: I started a git bisect. Suspicious PR: #8423 altered fused-op selection heuristics (short-seq preference). Bisecting now.

priya: Quick logs from canary-3:
```
$ ./perf-collector --node canary-3 --since 02:00
avg_batch=2.1  # baseline 4.8
kv_hit=0.64    # baseline 0.98
attn_kernel=attn_v2_fused
```

akash: lucas — can you generate a flamegraph for the decode path? If the attn kernel changed for long sequences that's unexpected.

lucas: Flamegraph uploaded: https://perf/redwood/fg/1718002468. Top hot spots: `kv_memcopy` and `attn_v2_fused::tail_dispatch`. Also seeing a lot of branch-mispredict samples around the selector.

emma: Reproduced locally: reverting PR #8423 restores p95 and kv_hit to baseline. Bisect points to 8423 as the regression-introducer.

lucas: Confirmed with `git bisect` + bench: `runtime/bench/decode/regression_long_seq`. PR #8423 adds an extra memcpy along the kernel selection path when `seq > 512 && batch_size <= 3`. That memcpy plus a new alignment step increases tail overhead for long sequences with small batches.

priya: Proposed immediate mitigation: guard fused-op selection with `if (avg_batch >= BATCH_THRESH) { prefer_fused = true } else { prefer_fused = false }` and drop the memcpy. I'll draft a hotfix PR for canary.

akash: Rollout remains PAUSED. This is P0 — don't resume canary until we validate fix. If hotfix looks good we can canary it on a tiny subset.

release-bot: Canaries on hold. Manual approval required to resume affected groups.

ci-bot: Triggered perf job for hotfix branch (runtime/hotfix/kernel-selection). Expected runtime ~20m, will post summary when done.

lucas: Additional note — the fused path change also altered memory alignment for KV buffers which reduced prefix reuse heuristics; that helps explain the drop in kv_hit. So two effects: memcpy + alignment -> lower reuse + more copy overhead.

emma: Adding to the incident draft: root cause = kernel-selection heuristic in PR #8423 that favored fused kernels in regimes it shouldn't have (small batch + long seq), introduced extra memcpy and alignment change. Mitigations: hotfix revert/guard, CI perf test that checks kv_hit and avg_batch for regression, add unit test covering selector behavior for batch sizes 1-4 and seq 256/512/1024.

akash: Thanks. priya — when you open the hotfix PR, tag it with `hotfix/regression` and drop the link here. I'll coordinate rollback if CI-hotfix still shows a regression.

priya: Hotfix PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/8480 — removes the memcpy and adds the avg_batch guard + a regression test. CI perf job (hotfix branch) is already posting: initial numbers show p95 back to baseline on the canary branch.

release-bot: Manual approval requested for hotfix merge. Tagging oncall_release.

akash: I approve merging to canary-rollback-track after the CI perf job and one smoke run on a single node. I'll monitor overnight.

priya: Will follow-up with a short postmortem draft once we have CI artifacts.

lucas: Follow-up investigation item: add a perf unit test that validates no extra memcpy introduced in selection path and assert kv buffer alignment unchanged by selector.

emma: Good catch everyone. Lesson: kernel selection heuristics are subtle — we need stronger perf guardrails for low-batch cases. :+1:

akash: Closing loop: once hotfix is stable we'll unpause rollout with canary fraction 1%. If regression resurfaces we revert 5.1.2-rc and roll back changes on release track.
